title: Henry VII (1457–1509) — Breton Exile, Bosworth Field, and the Ledger of Iron

teenKit.tldr: An exiled nobody seized the English throne and weaponized the legal system by backdating his reign by 24 hours. This instantly turned every political rival into a traitor, letting him legally rob them without starting a civil war.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that whoever controls the definition of the rules holds ultimate power, showing how bureaucratic systems can be deadlier than physical weapons.
keyTakeaways: Henry VII used an obscure legal weapon called an Act of Attainder to wipe out his enemies' property rights and inheritances overnight.
By backdating his reign to the day before the battle, he legally reframed his opponents from defending a king into committing treason against an already-crowned ruler.
Instead of executing his rivals and triggering endless blood feuds, he forced them to buy back their freedom and estates through expensive, terrified obedience.

vocab.meaning: A legislative weapon that strips individuals of their property, titles, and civil rights without a trial.
A legal penalty that prevents a convicted traitor's children from ever inheriting land, money, or titles.
A system of politics based on practical, ruthless power and tactical advantages rather than moral or ideological principles.
The highest social class of nobility, consisting of lords, barons, and dukes who held vast lands and private armies.

quiz.question: Why did Henry VII backdate his official start date to the day before the Battle of Bosworth?
options: To accurately reflect the date he arrived in England
To legally classify everyone who fought against him as a traitor
To avoid paying taxes on his coronation ceremony
To honor the soldiers who died during the voyage
quiz.explanation: Backdating his reign made anyone who fought under the previous king retroactively guilty of treason.

quiz.question: What was the primary advantage of using an Act of Attainder instead of executing rebellious lords?
options: It avoided triggering new blood feuds and violent rebellions while still emptying their war chests.
It allowed the lords to keep their titles if they apologized in public.
It was cheaper than maintaining a prison system.
It required the approval of an independent jury.
quiz.explanation: Wiping out opponents legally rather than killing them in masses prevented their families from starting immediate revenge wars.

quiz.question: How did wealthy lords eventually regain their lands and standing under Henry VII's system?
options: By winning a duel against the king's champions
By discovering hidden gold mines in Wales
By buying back royal mercy through years of impeccable, terrified service
By appealing their case to foreign courts
quiz.explanation: Henry turned royal mercy into an expensive commodity that had to be earned back through strict obedience and cash.
